rejectionReason: copilot-pr-merged-report is a pure analytics/reporting workflow: at adoption (commit 0d53b1fcfa831bbe0da078b9729b33bbb3221064, PR #5569, 2025-12-04) and unchanged today, its only action is to summarize Copilot PRs that already merged autonomously in the prior 24 hours and publish that summary as a discussion. The workflow does not create, resolve, or own any repository opportunity (no issue/PR is opened, fixed, reviewed, or otherwise changed by the run), so there is no attained repository outcome to bind a run to. The only observable signals are whether a report discussion was published, how many PRs/lines/test files it tallied, and how accurately it restated numbers already present in the PR/API data it read. Each of these is activity, output volume, or a re-derivation of already-computed data rather than a direct operational outcome, and the operational-value contract explicitly excludes activity, output volume, traces, and agent judgment as substitutes for attainment. No comparable pre-adoption evidence or opportunity exists either, since the workflow itself is the sole reporting mechanism being evaluated. Because no direct, defensible primary metric in [0,1] can be constructed without substituting one of these excluded proxies, this design is blocked rather than accepted or rejected on a specific formula.

decisions.selected: Adoption-time intent recovered from PR #5569 (commit 0d53b1fcfa831bbe0da078b9729b33bbb3221064): generate a daily summary of Copilot PRs merged in the prior 24 hours (merged-PR count, lines added/deleted, test files touched, workflow run timing) and publish it as an 'audits' discussion. No corrective, remediation, or acceptance action is specified for the run itself.
alternatives: Treat the workflow as accountable for the code/test quality of the Copilot PRs it summarizes
Treat the workflow as responsible for triggering follow-up remediation on flagged PRs
decisions.rationale: The adoption PR title/body ('Add daily report generation for copilot pull requests') and the workflow's unchanged Mission section describe only report generation; no follow-up action, gate, or state change on the summarized PRs is ever performed by this workflow.

decisions.selected: No repository opportunity (issue, PR, or otherwise) is created, resolved, or owned by a run; the run's only artifact is a discussion summarizing PRs that already merged before the run started.
alternatives: Bind each run to the set of Copilot PRs merged in the preceding 24 hours and score attainment of a per-PR outcome such as continued PR mergeability
Bind each run to its scheduled reporting slot and score whether a report discussion appears for that period
decisions.rationale: The PRs being summarized are already merged and closed by the time the run executes, so the run cannot influence their outcome; treating 'a report exists for the period' as the opportunity reduces to scoring output volume, which the contract excludes.

decisions.selected: No accepted repository evidence exists beyond the discussion the workflow itself creates and the already-merged PR data it reads; both are activity/output produced by or for the run rather than an outcome attained on an external opportunity.
alternatives: Score discussion-creation success (a report was published) as accepted evidence
Score numeric accuracy of the report's line/test counts by re-querying the same PR API data the workflow already read
decisions.rationale: Discussion-creation success is output volume (a safe-output side effect), and re-deriving the same PR statistics to check accuracy only restates activity the workflow already performed; neither constitutes independent evidence of a repository outcome.

decisions.selected: No direct primary metric in [0,1] is defensible for this workflow; every candidate signal available (report published, PR/line/test counts tallied, report numeric accuracy, discussion engagement) is activity, output volume, a restatement of already-computed data, or an agent-judgment proxy, all of which the operational-value contract excludes.
alternatives: Binary metric: did the run publish a report discussion
Accuracy metric: recomputed PR statistics compared to the report's stated numbers
Engagement metric: views/comments on the published discussion as a proxy for usefulness
decisions.rationale: Report-published and PR/line/test counts are output volume; recomputed accuracy re-derives the same activity rather than measuring an attained repository outcome; engagement metrics are indirect popularity/agent-perception proxies, not direct attainment evidence. No formulation avoids these exclusions.

uncertainties.description: The workflow's stated deliverable is a scheduled analytics report; it never intervenes on repository state, so no repository outcome is attributable to a run beyond its own reporting activity.
Even accuracy or engagement metrics on the published report would reflect reporting quality or audience reaction, not a repository outcome caused by the workflow's run.

Because the PRs summarized are already merged before the run starts, there is no deterministic way to bind a run to a single opportunity it could still influence, making assignment ambiguous rather than a design choice that could be frozen.
